A `{#snippet children()}` without parameters directly inside a component does what its content does without the snippet: Svelte passes the content as `children`. The rule looks at components under Svelte 5.

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. It runs on the Svelte components that an ESLint config lints with `svelte-eslint-parser`, in the place of the rule of `eslint-plugin-svelte`:

{/* skip */}

```js eslint.config.js
import svelte from "eslint-plugin-svelte";

export default [
  ...svelte.configs.recommended,
  { rules: { "svelte/no-useless-children-snippet": "error" } },
];
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}

```svelte
<Card>
  {#snippet children()}
    <p>Saved</p>
  {/snippet}
</Card>
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}

```svelte
<Card>
  <p>Saved</p>
</Card>
```
